{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Flatbread|Flatbread]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistani cuisine]]

'''Bhatoora''' is a light and airy [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] fried [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], and it is generally eaten with a [[Cookbook:Chickpea|chickpea]] [[Cookbook:Curry|curry]] or [[Cookbook:Cholley|cholle]]. 

==Ingredients==

*5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (650 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 1.4 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|wheat flour]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*½ tsp active dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]] OR 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Ghee|ghee]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 cup (275 g / 9.7 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]

==Procedure==

# Sift together the flour and salt.
# Mix the yeast with ½ cup lukewarm water, and keep aside for 10 minutes.
# Mix the ghee and sugar with the flour. Add the yoghurt and dissolved yeast or the baking soda. A little more lukewarm water may be added if necessary. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] well until the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] becomes soft and pliable. Use a little oil to knead well. 
# Cover it with a wet cloth and keep aside for 4 hours.
# Heat the ghee in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]].
# Make the dough into small balls. [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the balls out very thin.
# [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep fry]] the dough in hot ghee until golden brown. The dough should puff up a lot and develop a large airy pocket inside.
# Remove from the oil, and serve hot with ''channa'' or ''choley'' (chickpea curry).

==See also==
* [[Cookbook:North Indian Fermented Bread (Batooru)|Batooru]]
